o1.biggest_strength: It covers the full WhatsApp system the owner asked for, including COD confirmation, cart recovery, shipped/out-for-delivery updates, after-hours automation, and a useful weekly scorecard.
o1.biggest_mistake: The prepaid nudge is too generic and has no incentive or stronger Tier 3 treatment, even though Tier 3 is the main RTO cost driver.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add pincode-risk-based prepaid/advance rules with offer economics, and tighten template categorisation so anything promotional is clearly Marketing.

o2.biggest_strength: It puts the money problem first, correctly shows Tier 3 as the biggest RTO cost driver, and builds the COD hold/prepaid nudge flow around that risk.
o2.biggest_mistake: It leaves a few operational details to confirm and the after-hours automation is less fully built out than it could be.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the after-hours bot flow and all template button structures fully submission-ready, with no remaining confirmation list.

reason: Output 2 is the one I would rather run because it targets the expensive Tier 3 RTO problem, sizes the prepaid offer against refusal cost, and gives a cleaner rollout. Output 1 is strong and more complete in some template coverage, but it misses the highest-leverage prepaid/RTO targeting move.
